text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Wednesday:
- Europay (Switzerland) and Telekurs started a four-month pilot project that allows credit card payments to be made safely via the Internet.
- Rail Gourmet, a subsidiary of SAirRelations, is acquiring Britain's European Rail Catering (ERC) Group.
- Swiss hearing-aid manufacturer Phonak strengthens its position on the Italian market with the takeover of Italy's hearing aid distributor Decibel in Milan on July 1.
- Patrick Heiniger, 46, is taking over his father Andre Heiniger's position as head of the board of directors of Geneva-based watch maker Rolex.

- Swiss television will air the controversial BBC documentary "Nazi Gold and Jewish Money" tomorrow night. The documentary claims that Italian Jews were transported through Switzerland to concentration camps in Eastern Europe during World War Two.
- Maag Holding AG sold its subsidiary Burkland Holding to the Textron Group in the U.S.

- Four metal building firms in Mendrisiotto in the Italian speaking region of Switzerland will most likely shut down due to lack of business and some 40 employees will lose their jobs at the end of August.
- Oerlikon Contraves plans to increase operating results from 48 million Swiss francs (1996) to over 70 million francs by the year 2000.
- The Swiss postal service and Swiss Bank Corp are launching an investment fund called the "Yellow Funds" for small investments, starting September at all 3,700 Swiss post offices.
